speaker: 说话人1
content: The thing for me that was the most fascinating about this story is that we as human beings we all want to count for something come from somewhere and to belong. Whether it's a family, a cult, a religion, a group of friends, whatever it is we all want to belong somewhere. And that is what this film is about. It's about establishing these five different factions, families. And you have to choose to belong.

speaker: 说话人1
content: And if you don't or if you're cut from your faction, you are nobody, which is I think everyone's fear. It's all of our fear, you know, that we will be ostracized from society or friendship or a class or a group or something. And we fear, you know, I think as human beings, we do naturally fear being left out or other people's judgment, you know. It's, and I think it's hard in the world that we live today with so much media exposure, I think available to young kids. And so much in terms of the viral world and

speaker: 说话人1
content: phones and iPads and all of this stuff that pairing it all back and just being a person, being an individual, I think is even more challenging for kids now than it was for me when I was 16 years old. And so to me this film is really striking because it's very much about belonging somewhere and making that choice and making that commitment and there's a hell of a lot to be said for that, you know, there's a very basic values. So that's why I think that it is in some way quite different to a lot of the franchise pieces that have been out in the last five years because it has a very strong fundamental sort of moral message, I think, at its core. That doesn't necessarily mean it's better, it just means it's different. And for me that was the most interesting thing about this.
